headline: A 2019 law lets the FAA's sitting Deputy Administrator keep the job even when the FAA Administrator is a former regular military officer.
what_it_does: The law applies to the Deputy Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration who was serving on the day the law was enacted. That person may be an active-duty military officer, or a retired or former officer. The law lets that person keep serving as deputy administrator even if the FAA Administrator is a former regular officer of the Armed Forces.

who_it_affects.group: The FAA Deputy Administrator serving on August 2, 2019
who_it_affects.how: This person may continue in the deputy role even though the FAA Administrator is a former regular military officer.
The agency's leadership arrangement for that deputy position is allowed to continue as it was on the date of enactment.
